summary.text: Visa and Mastercard let any registered developer create a project and call a sandbox the same day, and production waits on a contract or company verification.
American Express reviews every product request before keys appear, and Discover's Developer Center admits developers only by a representative's invitation.

The ISO 8583 host specifications that acquirers build to are marked confidential at all four networks. The networks distribute them behind Visa Online, Mastercard Connect, the Amex Knowledge Base or EASI.

Host certification is representative-led everywhere. Discover and American Express hand out forms and test plans through a named manager, and Mastercard needs licensed simulators ordered on Mastercard Connect.

Token services are the least self-serve surface. Visa's VTS page routes to an account executive or acquirer, MDES issuer work runs through a Mastercard delivery manager, and Amex notification tests need a representative.
Processors and programme managers carry most integration for smaller partners. Host testing runs once per platform, and Marqeta certifies each network release for all its clients.
Discover's strongest public asset is twelve readable OpenAPI specifications on the Partner Product Portal, but the credentials, test cases and certification behind them are released by people.
The public record is thin for PULSE, which publishes no developer portal, API reference or interface specification.

by_partner.partner_type: Developers building on network APIs (independent developers, fintech engineering teams, integrators)

how_it_works.text: A developer registers on developer.visa.com with name, email, organisation and company website, then signs in through Visa's Universal Login with MFA or a passkey.
From the dashboard the developer clicks Add new project, names it, picks an API such as Visa Transaction Controls, selects 'Generate a CSR for me' and clicks Create project.
A pop-up then offers the certificate private key, which can be downloaded only once.
The Credentials tab shows the project client certificate, common certificates including the Visa Developer Platform root, and a user ID and password for HTTP Basic authentication.
The first call is Hello World over Two-Way SSL, tested in Postman or in SoapUI after building a keystore with OpenSSL.
Each API authenticates with Two-Way SSL or X-Pay Token, and some add message level encryption with JWE.
Mock test data sits in a Test Data table per API inside the project, and it never touches VisaNet.
Restricted products carry a lock and need a Request Access application that a Visa admin reviews before the API can join a project.
To go live the developer opens Going live in the project, registers the company or enters a Visa BID, adds contacts and beneficial owners, and describes the use case.
A product team reviews the request with no stated timeline, then sends a contract with pricing and terms.
Certification and production credentials need a new CSR per environment and appear only after signature, behind an emailed one-time password.

friction.text: The private key can be downloaded only once, so a lost key means a new project.
APIs cannot be removed from a sandbox project, so a wrong pick also means a new project.
SDKs, sample code and implementation guides are downloads behind sign-in.
Visa says onboarding can take two weeks or several months, and its product team states no review timeline.
Visa says timing is the first question on nearly every client's mind.
No numeric rate limits are published and load testing is prohibited.

how_it_works.text: A developer signs up with email, password, name, company and country, verifies the email and logs in.
On My Projects the developer clicks Create new project, enters details, says whether the project is built for a client, selects APIs and clicks Proceed.
The portal generates credentials, often a consumer key and an RSA key pair made in the browser, and Open Project starts Sandbox testing.
Mastercard's own video shows sandbox keys on the dashboard straight after project creation.
Most services use OAuth 1.0a with RSA-SHA256 signing, and a few use OAuth 2.0 with FAPI 2.0 or mutual TLS.
The quick start offers three routes: an API tool such as Postman or Insomnia, Mastercard SDK samples, or a client generated from the downloadable OpenAPI spec.
Before production the developer verifies the company, instant when linked to Mastercard Connect or a Company ID, and declares commercial countries.
Request Production access generates credentials at once, and they activate only after Mastercard approves.

There is no portal-wide set of test cards, and some products need a representative to configure them.
Keys expire after 13 months, and two documents disagree on the reminder schedule.
Direct support tickets need sign-in.

how_it_works.text: A developer clicks Sign Up, creates an Amex OneID login and sets a six-to-nine-digit security code.
On My Projects the developer clicks Add Project, and the Project Dashboard lists To Do items: certificate upload, OAuth details and a questionnaire.
The product then sits in Requested until Amex approves it, and only then do the Client ID and Client Secret appear.
Partner applications use mutual TLS with Amex-signed certificates from an uploaded CSR, plus OAuth 2 or HMAC request signing.
An Approved sandbox integration shows a Move to Production link, which reopens the To Do list and a second review.

friction.text: No product offers instant sandbox access, although the documentation says some do.
Five products hide their specification behind an invitation.
The Java and .NET SDKs are header helpers last updated in 2020 and 2018.
The portal's What's New log stopped in May 2024.

how_it_works.text: The Developer Center home at developer.discover.com is a login gate with one link to the Partner Product Portal.
A new developer fills in the Contact Us form and waits for a Discover representative to send an invitation.
Discover's own guide says partners self-register, then says access is by invitation only.
After approval Discover creates a Developer Center organisation and an application with client credentials and a Sandbox, Certification or Prod API Plan.
The same process repeats for production and issues new credentials.
Requests carry an OAuth 2 token plus an X-DFS-API-PLAN header, and many APIs add a second factor, mutual TLS and JWE or JWS payload protection.
The Partner Product Portal publishes an OpenAPI document for each of its twelve products to signed-out readers.

tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Twelve products in six groups, each with Overview and API Specs tabs.

tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A Business Users Guide with a four-phase activity table and a twelve-section Developers Guide on registration, keys, OAuth and encryption.

tools_and_screens.name: Developer Center FAQ and Contact Us
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Answers that route every new user to a representative.

friction.text: Developer Center documentation pages return 403 to signed-out readers.
No sandbox is reachable without an invitation, and no changelog, status page or llms.txt was found.
The Consumer Application Certificate downloads only once, and a replacement needs a request.
Rate limits come from a per-partner API Plan and are not published.

how_it_works.text: UnionPay's Open Platform signs members in with their institution portal account and pre-fills onboarding tasks with data UnionPay holds.
Its test tasks are generated from the project's confirmed business, technical and network information.

tools_and_screens.name: UnionPay Open Platform project
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Project nodes that activate once a support manager is assigned, with test reports linked from the testing platform.

friction.text: A new project's steps stay inactive until the local office assigns a project support manager.

best_pattern.text: Mastercard gives the shortest path to a first call. It pairs a same-day sandbox with open markdown docs and an MCP server, and keys the production gate to an existing client identity.

discover_today.text: Discover publishes readable OpenAPI specifications but gates the sandbox behind a representative's invitation, so a developer cannot make a first call unaided. Inference: the Partner Product Portal already has projects and credentials switched on to build from.

by_partner.partner_type: Acquirers, acquirer processors and gateways (host integration and certification)

how_it_works.text: A member that uses a processor submits a regional client information questionnaire, and a non-member processor signs a VisaNet Letter of Agreement before touching V.I.P. or BASE II.
Large acquiring platforms hire engineers to build Visa and Mastercard authorisation and clearing flows in ISO 8583.
VisaNet documentation is confidential, and members must stop staff sharing it with third parties.
BASE I, the V.I.P. authorisation format, is ISO 8583:1987 with many Visa additions, according to a third-party tooling site.
For chip host certification the acquirer establishes a project with Visa and pulls host test scripts from Visa Online.
Terminal testing connects to the Visa Certification Management Service or a Visa-confirmed simulator, and a completion letter closes host testing.
Visa's newer VisaNet Connect Acceptance offers a REST authorisation API on ISO 20022, with no ISO 8583 mapping on its public pages.
Each Visa guide names the Business Enhancements release it reflects. Changes arrive through Global Technical Letters and Implementation Guides.
A centre must sign off from VisaNet whenever its authorisation system is down.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Online, now Visa Access
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: The gated client site holding host test scripts, risk standards and service enrolment, granted at BID level.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Digital Partner Services
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Approval Services Portal and Tap to Phone Certification Portal for chip product testing.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa testing guides
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Client versions of the VCMS V.I.P. Testing Guide, VCMS Testing Guide for BASE II and VisaNet Testing Guide.

friction.text: Level 3 testing is mandatory and separate from vendor approvals.
Several POS systems, devices and acquirers multiply the certifications one software version needs.
Visa Ready Tap to Phone certification takes 6 to 12 months with lab costs of USD 50,000 or more, by Visa's own account.
Key exchange fails unless Visa lists the institution as a Dynamic Key Exchange participant.
A first subscription to an optional file such as the enhanced TC 33 capture file triggers full implementation activities.

how_it_works.text: Mastercard's rules point customers to the Customer Interface Specification, Single Message System Specifications and IPM Clearing Formats manuals.
Those manuals and bulletins live in the Technical Resource Center on Mastercard Connect, which needs an account set up through a Mastercard representative.
Connections run through Mastercard-owned equipment such as the Mastercard Interface Processor.
Host validation (NIV) tests the ISO 8583 interface using a licensed Mastercard simulator ordered from the Simulator Suite on Mastercard Connect.
An implementation project manager builds each session's case list, and the Test Selection Engine builds terminal plans from the configuration.
Mastercard also serves a public 64-page mapping from an ISO 20022 authorisation response to ISO 8583 data elements.
File Express is ordered in the Connect Store. The company's Security Administrator approves, then Mastercard, and each user needs a SecurID.
The CIS is reissued with a summary of changes since the last edition. Changes carry release names such as 10.2 or 19.Q2.

friction.text: Connect sign-in needs a User ID and an RSA SecurID token.
M-TIP Self-Approval and Fast Track let enrolled acquirers approve terminals themselves or reuse another acquirer's approval.
Readers find specification changes by searching the PDF for *chg* markers.
Hosts must process new DE 48 subelements that Mastercard has not announced.

how_it_works.text: Network Specifications ship as confidential manuals twice a year, in April and October, on signing an agreement.
Merchant and processor specifications such as GCAG sit on the password-protected merchantspecs site, and changes are announced six months ahead in a NOSC.
Host certification is eight steps: the acquirer says it is ready, Amex opens a project, assigns a resource, reviews the plan and specs, and issues a certification summary.
Amex's ATS host simulator is free, and other simulators must meet its approved provider rules.

tools_and_screens.name: Knowledge Base
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: The gated gateway to specifications, Participant Directory and service enrolment, with a three-business-day access turnaround.

tools_and_screens.name: merchantspecs login
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Technical specifications and BIN files for merchants and processors.

friction.text: No specification is public, and the certification page gates specs behind Knowledge Base.

how_it_works.text: The published on-ramp is EASI: click Join Now, enter contact and company details, invite colleagues, state a business purpose, verify and submit.
Discover says the EASI team typically reviews registration within two business days, then emails credentials.
EASI holds Program Documents, technical specifications and test card requests, and the fuller IIN table needs an NDA on file.
For D-PAS host certification the acquirer connects to Discover's test simulator and files a Host Certification Request Form, from which Discover assigns cases.
Every form comes from a Discover implementation manager, and certificate authority keys can arrive by encrypted email.
Acquirers see simulator results as they test and need not submit test logs.
PULSE offers one message format to many POS and ATM networks through its gateway, but publishes no specification.
In 2011 Discover posted its Technical Specifications on its website. Updates came each April and October with at least 30 days' notice.
Data links had to be redundant, and planned maintenance needed 72 hours' notice.

friction.text: Personal email addresses are rejected at EASI registration.
Certification forms and test keys need a person at Discover.
Moving to a platform with a different message format brings the networks back into testing.

best_pattern.text: Discover's own host simulator already shows acquirers results as they test and drops test-log submission, which is the most self-serve certification step found.

discover_today.text: Discover runs a self-registering EASI with a stated two-day review, but its certification forms and keys still pass through an implementation manager.

by_partner.partner_type: Payment facilitators, ISOs, ISVs and technology partners

how_it_works.text: Visa Acceptance, the former CyberSource developer centre, offers a public sandbox form and emails test credentials.
It publishes test card numbers and amount triggers for declines, with processor-specific guides.
Technology partners register through a separate form and a Visa team member then follows up.
Go-live and MID configuration are requested in the gated Business Center.
Agents register once per acquirer on Visa Partner and receive a TPA Business ID.

tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Sandbox, API reference with live console, SDKs in six languages, testing guide and response codes.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Acceptance status page
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public component status with email, SMS and feed subscriptions.

friction.text: Visa Acceptance warns that its sandbox can be unstable with 502 and 504 timeouts.
Two branded portals, Visa Acceptance and CyberSource, cover one platform.

how_it_works.text: Network Enablement Partners enrol for a direct Mastercard relationship in several tiers, listed on a public registry.
Engage lists qualified implementation partners, and its directory sits behind the developer login.
Transit systems integrators join the Transit Partner Program and receive Mastercard documents after signing the Transit Partner Agreement.
The Customer Delivery team leads transit projects. The plan covers payment model, suppliers, risk parameters, message data, testing and certification, and milestones.
Terminal vendors start design review early and receive a Letter of Approval after contactless type approval.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercard Gateway integration guides
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Regional public guides for Hosted Checkout, Hosted Session and Direct Payment, with test cards.

friction.text: Merchant Cloud appears on the developer portal as documentation only, with no API or sandbox.

how_it_works.text: The Integrated Payments Providers Program gives ISOs, ISVs, VARs and PSP aggregators specs, a relationship manager and certification under NDA.
Its five steps are register online, accept terms, enrol users, open the AMEX Enabled Dashboard, then test and certify.
Test cards and certification requests go to a Payment Vendor Relations mailbox.

tools_and_screens.name: AMEX Enabled Dashboard
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Step-by-step certification journey, document library, Messaging Center and DocuSign contracting.

friction.text: Registration is not approval, and each product must still pass certification.

how_it_works.text: EASI self-registration lists payment facilitators, ISOs and ISVs among its company types.
Type-approved products appear in a public Partner Directory of 43 entries.

tools_and_screens.name: Web Merchant Boarding
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A gated boarding link listed on Partner Resources.

friction.text: Terminal end-to-end certification runs through accredited service providers.

best_pattern.text: Visa Acceptance's open sandbox form, published test cards and public status page let a software vendor test without a sales conversation.

discover_today.text: Discover lets payfacs and ISVs self-register on EASI but publishes no sandbox or test cards for them.

by_partner.partner_type: Large issuers (token services, issuer host and product certification)

how_it_works.text: Under Visa's rules an issuer using VTS owns cardholder identity checks, provisioning decisions and credential updates.
The VTS developer page offers no sandbox and sends readers to an account executive, acquirer or Visa Ready, and its documentation is restricted.
A 2014 Visa deck for credit unions routed VTS information, a draft participation agreement and training to Visa Online.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Online
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: VTS service descriptions, FAQs and participation agreement, per the 2014 deck.

friction.text: None of the VTS enrolment screens is public.

how_it_works.text: Issuers start MDES Pre-Digitization by adding it to a portal project and asking a Customer Delivery Manager to open a Customer Integration Services project.
The issuer API has no sandbox and runs only in the Mastercard Test Facility and production.
Issuer endpoints are configured on Mastercard Developers at Customer ID level.
Before MTF testing the issuer sends an Excel file of test case IDs, requests and responses to the CIS representative.
MDES Customer Service follows a five-step path from sandbox to MTF and production.
Issuer files use separate bulk IDs for MTF and production. A Customer Implementation Services specialist sets up each new file.

tools_and_screens.name: MDES documentation set
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Getting Started, Configuring Services, Testing with test data preparation and result submission, release notes.

friction.text: Test evidence travels as a spreadsheet by email.
The issuer test case book is reissued with a change summary, so an issuer must recheck which cases apply.

how_it_works.text: Issuers must complete host and payment product certification with Amex test tools and custom test plans.
The Token Requester Management Portal is applied for after Knowledge Base access is granted.

tools_and_screens.name: Knowledge Base, Request Additional Services
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Where existing users add FraudNet, OpsNet, File Tracker and the Token Requester Management Portal.

friction.text: Every tool beyond the Knowledge Base is a further application.

how_it_works.text: DDX gives issuers one connection to Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay and Garmin Pay and network tokens for stored credentials.
Its APIs sit in the invitation-only Developer Center.
Implementation runs four phases: certification boarding, certification, production boarding and end-to-end testing, with Discover's team boarding each client profile.
Diners Club issuer resources sit on a separate ServiceNow instance for current issuers.

tools_and_screens.name: Issuer Card Account Services
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A public OpenAPI spec for issuer card updates using the ICAS_CARDUPDATE_V1 scope.

friction.text: Discover supplies test cases during certification boarding, and partners cannot fetch them themselves.

best_pattern.text: Mastercard publishes the MDES issuer path, its test steps and release notes openly, even though the work itself runs through a delivery manager.

discover_today.text: Discover documents its issuer phases and ICAS spec publicly, and every step past reading needs a Discover person.

how_it_works.text: Visa built an 'On Behalf Of' VTS enrolment for issuers and readied the CSCU and FIS platforms, per a 2014 deck a credit union organisation republished.
Associate members hold their own licence but rely on a principal for settlement and reporting.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Online product enrolment portal
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Where community issuers enrol in programmes.

friction.text: A community bank told the FDIC that debit tokenisation stalled while it waited on its core provider.

how_it_works.text: PULSE processes Discover Debit, Mastercard and Visa debit programmes through one point of access.
PULSE portal registration is a form with credentials promised within five business days.
Processor support runs through a named mailbox.

tools_and_screens.name: PULSE secure website
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: PULSE Debit Dashboard, ATM List Manager, Marketing Hub and PULSE Exchange behind one login.

friction.text: PULSE publishes no API reference or sandbox.

best_pattern.text: Issuer processors that certify each network release once and tell clients no action is needed remove build work from small issuers.

discover_today.text: PULSE already acts as a processor and gateway for small issuers. Inference: Discover's build experience for these institutions is PULSE's and the core provider's.

by_partner.partner_type: Fintechs and programme managers (via issuer processors and sponsors)

how_it_works.text: Visa describes a sponsor model of BIN sponsor, issuer processor and programme manager, and Visa Ready lists certified processors.
Thredd sets out five steps: sign up with the network, complete its forms, configure the processor, test, then finish wallet certification.
Visa and the processor exchange JWE and JWS public certificates during the implementation project.
Visa sends Thredd 100 to 200 new token requestor updates a month, and Thredd applies them without client input.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Partner directory
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Certified partners filterable by country.

friction.text: Visa's going-live form asks whether the project will be resold or white-labelled.

how_it_works.text: Since May 2025 a principal needs Mastercard approval before sponsoring a programme manager.
Marqeta documents certification against each quarterly Mastercard release for its clients.
For MDES a programme manager can add a phone to MTF, which connects to Thredd's test environment.

friction.text: Networks send processors change documents four times a year.
Thredd's standard token set-up needs no network testing, while custom features need a separate processor project.
Many Thredd clients test in production instead of wiring up network test services.

how_it_works.text: Amex admits processors such as Lithic and Marqeta to its Agile Partnership Platform so their fintech clients can issue without a direct licence.

friction.text: American Banker reports Amex stresses selectivity in this route.

how_it_works.text: Discover describes a sponsor model and names no processor on its fintech page.
Marqeta certifies Discover releases, while Stripe, Adyen and Lithic issuing document no Discover issuing.

friction.text: SoFi Tech Solutions says a programme's primary network is usually Mastercard or Visa.

best_pattern.text: Processor mandate logs, such as Marqeta's and SoFi's, translate each network release into client impact.

discover_today.text: Discover reaches fintechs only where a processor has built for it, and several leading issuing platforms have not.

by_partner.partner_type: Merchants, wallets and other token requestors

how_it_works.text: Visa Acceptance's partner model boards a merchant by API, then asks the partner to email merchant details to support to enable network tokens.
Visa Acceptance sends the request to each card brand, which returns a token requestor ID.

tools_and_screens.name: Token Management Service guide
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Network Token Enablement, Partner Model onboarding, Token Requestor IDs and webhook subscriptions.

friction.text: An email step sits in the middle of an otherwise API-driven flow.

Merchant tokenisation is sold directly or through PSPs.

friction.text: Existing merchant integrations must migrate before the retirement date.

how_it_works.text: The Amex Token Service guide is readable signed out and publishes sample test cards.
Testing token notifications needs a representative to register the merchant's endpoint, certificates and IP addresses.

tools_and_screens.name: Amex Token Service API reference
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Six endpoints including provisionings, purchasetokens and outbound notifications, HMAC security and a spec download.

friction.text: Sandbox does not save token state, so lifecycle tests always return Active.

how_it_works.text: Stored Token Services needs OAuth 2 with a second-factor JWT and JWE encryption.
Token requestors must expose a webhook endpoint for issuer notifications.
PULSE's Side-by-Side token service is enrolled by a contact form.

tools_and_screens.name: Discover Stored Token Services API Specs tab
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A public OpenAPI 3.0.1 document with operations such as getCardAsset and lcmNotifications.

friction.text: No retry or signing detail is published for the notification webhook.

best_pattern.text: Amex publishes token test cards in the guide itself, which lets a merchant test provisioning without a request.

discover_today.text: Discover's token API is fully specified in public, and it adds a second-factor JWT and JWE encryption on top of OAuth.

how_it_works.text: Network rules require any sender of ATM transactions to be a bank or a bank-approved processor.
Level 3 terminal testing covers ATMs, and it is the acquirer's responsibility.
Operators work in their processor's web platform for set-up, alerts and cash forecasting.
The processor relays network rules and warns of suspension and fines.

tools_and_screens.name: PULSE ATM List Manager
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A gated PULSE tool for ATM listings.

friction.text: Operators meet networks second-hand through processors and sponsors.

best_pattern.text: No network was found offering ATM operators a direct build surface, so the processor portal is the pattern.

discover_today.text: PULSE offers ATM acquirers a gated ATM List Manager and no public technical path.

design_moves.title: A sandbox key on the first visit
design_moves.move: Let a signed-up developer create a project, get sandbox credentials and published test cards, and call the twelve existing APIs without a representative.
design_moves.why_advantage: It reaches Visa and Mastercard parity and moves ahead of American Express's key review. It replaces Discover's invitation step, the largest gap found.

design_moves.title: Certification as a shared project record
design_moves.move: Generate the case list from the partner's stated configuration, collect results in the portal, and show who owns each step.
design_moves.why_advantage: Mastercard's MDES asks for an Excel file by email and Discover's forms come from a manager. UnionPay already links tests and confirmations in one project. Mastercard's issuer case tables already mark each case for simulator or MTF, which a record could turn into a checklist.

design_moves.title: Build for the processor as the customer
design_moves.move: Let a processor create projects on behalf of clients, manage them through an API, and show which clients inherit its certification.
design_moves.why_advantage: Host testing runs once per platform and processors already publish per-release impact. Among the portals read, Mastercard offers an 'on behalf of a client' flag and a portal API.

design_moves.title: Specifications by entitlement, versioned and diffable
design_moves.move: Serve the host specification to entitled users as searchable pages with a per-release change list, and publish a public field map for feasibility.
design_moves.why_advantage: All four networks gate specs as manuals, while Mastercard shows a public mapping works. Processors staff teams to turn releases into requirements. Mastercard marks changes with *chg* tags found by PDF search, and Discover posted specifications on its website in 2011.

design_moves.title: Token requestor onboarding without email
design_moves.move: Issue a token requestor ID and register notification endpoints in the portal, and route to PULSE Side-by-Side from the same flow.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa Acceptance, Amex and Mastercard each insert an email or representative step. Discover owns a routable debit token others lack.

design_moves.title: One entry for every Discover build surface
design_moves.move: Put the Developer Center, Partner Product Portal, EASI, Release Compliance Tool and Advanced Payments behind one sign-in and one project.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa and Mastercard link identities, and two Discover portals already share an identity provider. The study classes this as parity. It removes friction without giving a partner a reason to join.

design_moves.title: Credentials that do not strand the developer
design_moves.move: Allow re-download or self-service reissue of keys and certificates, with renewal reminders in every environment.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa and Discover make keys one-time downloads, and Visa reminds only certification and production projects. Mastercard now automates production mTLS certificates.

design_moves.title: Docs readable by coding assistants
design_moves.move: Publish llms.txt, markdown twins of each page and a documentation MCP server.
design_moves.why_advantage: Mastercard and Visa already do this, and Discover's portals return 404 or a bare title to a fetching tool.

design_moves.title: State the network's own service levels
design_moves.move: Show Discover's commitments on its own steps, such as registration review, and give each an escalation route.
design_moves.why_advantage: Discover already states a two-day EASI review and PULSE five days. Mastercard pairs its service levels with escalation channels.

design_moves.title: Public status and webhook contracts
design_moves.move: Publish API status per environment and document webhook retries, signing and subscriptions.
design_moves.why_advantage: Mastercard and Visa Acceptance run public status pages and document retries. Discover publishes no webhook retry detail, and no Discover status page was found.
